summary: No new execution this turn; the audit stands on its three supported findings and I only tightened the outer boundary of the newest one. Added the adoption-path sources (leader.rs:257-285 sync_log/take_max_promise_sync, follower.rs:13-51 the prepare-phase Promise log_sync) and rewrote the identity question's scope statement: what is witnessed is a false completion for an entry that was accepted only locally (its node isolated, never replicated), and the next information that would change the judgment is whether the same Ok(idx) can be reported when the caller's entry was accepted by a write quorum — the following leader is expected to adopt such a value before syncing anyone, so the Ok arm would then be truthful, and that expectation is directly testable by replicating the entry to a quorum before cutting the leader. Current position: (1) the runtime's event egress parks the actor loop and, with enough nodes parked, the cluster stops deciding (receipts ff4511e8, 76557a28); (2) the core has no timer-driven repair for a lost Accepted reply, so a quorum-accepted entry stays undecided for at least 100 resend periods in the 2-node case (receipt 092538c6); (3) append_notify can resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided at idx, shadowing the documented Superseded heuristic (receipt 743518e2). The limits carried for each remain as recorded (bounds witnessed at capacities 64/8 rather than the 1024 default; only the 2-node configuration probed for the core gap; the identity interleaving constructed rather than sampled).
